facts.function: Data Diode Device (first-named): enforces one-way transfer of data between networks of different security levels
facts.form: stand-alone network appliance; other listed products are a keyboard switch, a multiple computer (KVM) switch and software

gri_path: Several different articles named, not a GRI 3(b) set: classify the first-named, the Data Diode Device
GRI 1: heading 8517 covers other apparatus for the transmission or reception of data in a wired or wireless network; chapter 84 note 6(D) excludes such network transmission apparatus from 8471
GRI 6: 8517.62.00 machines for the reception, conversion and transmission of data; a data diode passes data one way but is not a modem or switching/routing apparatus, so suffix 90 other

rejected_alternatives.reason: switching and routing apparatus; the data diode does not switch or route traffic among multiple ports, it only enforces unidirectional transfer
units of ADP machines (used for KVM switches, N332683); excluded for network data transmission apparatus by chapter 84 note 6(D)
8517 more specifically covers network data transmission apparatus

classification.rationale: The description lists several distinct products that do not form a retail set, so the first-named, the Data Diode Device, is classified. A data diode receives and retransmits data between networks in one direction only, which is apparatus for the reception, conversion and transmission of data in heading 8517, subheading 8517.62; chapter 84 note 6(D) keeps it out of 8471. CBP places network data transceivers in 8517.62.0090 (NY N336394, in force); the KVM switches would go to 8471.80.10 separately (NY N332683).
